clue.text: Stand right back by music player

indicators.note: back tells us to read the abbreviation for right from end to start

parts.note: R or RT is a standard abbreviation for right
an iPod is Apple's portable music player

explanation.surface: Someone puts a stand behind their music player, on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' tells you to reverse the abbreviation for right before the music player; 'Stand' as a verb is the false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged support for a camera or kettle is a stand.

clue.text: Share of love dropped from speech

indicators.note: dropped from says one piece is taken away from the word for speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
love means nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A speech that has lost its share of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped from' removes O (love, tennis's zero) from ORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed allowance or portion handed out is a share.

clue.text: Passerine bird on horse

parts.note: passerines are the perching birds, so one is a percher
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small songbird sitting on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A Percheron is a heavy French draught horse breed.

clue.text: Start of letter from French fleet to monsieur? On the contrary

parts.note: de is French for from
an armada is a fleet of warships
M is the abbreviation of the French title Monsieur

explanation.surface: Opening a letter from the French navy to a gentleman, though really it is addressed to a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' is the joke: the letter is built from 'to monsieur' yet it greets a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The salutation used at the opening of a formal letter to a woman.

clue.text: 6 took precedence: if I go in get abused

parts.note: 6 written as a Roman numeral is VI

indicators.note: go in tells us the following words are placed inside the word for took precedence

parts.note: led means went first, took precedence
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Six people pushed to the front; if I barge in I'll be insulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go in' puts IF and I inside the word for took precedence, making LIFIED; the 6 is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To be vilified is to be spoken of with abuse and contempt.

clue.text: Setter's power to support tax on church centre

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax
the setter refers to themself as I
can means be able to, having the power

explanation.surface: The setter backs a tax on a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts I CAN under VAT, since this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the seat and headquarters of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Right of tenure when I go in and won't get up?

definitions.note: a description of the person rather than a noun; the question mark admits the stretch

indicators.note: go in shows the letter I is placed inside the word for a right of tenure

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid
taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal right to hold property, and someone refusing to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A morning spent staying in bed late is what someone has when they refuse to rise.

clue.text: She's dowdy — see note at bottom

parts.note: F is a musical note
rump is the backside, the bottom

explanation.surface: A remark that a woman is dowdy, with a note at the foot of the page.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer F sits above RUMP, the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A frump is a drab, unfashionably dressed woman.

clue.text: You need considerable dexterity and gold to get outside

indicators.note: considerable here means a large part of the word dexterity, its inner run, is used

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Getting outside demands great skill and money.
explanation.walkthrough: A considerable part of DEXTERITY is EXTERI, its first and last two letters dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Exterior means the outer side or surface of something.

clue.text: Horoscope the making of a popular play?

definitions.meaning: a reading of the stars cast for someone's birth

definitions.text: the making of a popular play?
definitions.meaning: a cast of famous actors that makes a show a hit

explanation.definitionFit: A forecast from the stars, and a line-up of celebrities that ensures a production succeeds.

clue.text: Justice for actors

definitions.meaning: The trade union for performers in the UK

explanation.definitionFit: Fairness in law, and the name of the British performers' trade union.

clue.text: Batsman and bowler? Yes, before lunch

definitions.text: Batsman and bowler? Yes, before lunch

parts.note: the answer to the question is yes, he was both
am means morning, the time before lunch

explanation.surface: A cricketer who can bat and bowl, active in the morning session.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Botham was a celebrated English cricket all-rounder, both batsman and bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: An England cricketer famed for being a top all-rounder with bat and ball.

clue.text: Plot against part of church

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a spire is the pointed tower of a church

explanation.surface: Scheming against part of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to scheme secretly together, to plot.

clue.text: Emetics do exactly this with knowledge

definitions.note: a verb phrase, matching the verb in the grid

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as exactly as written
ken means range of knowledge

explanation.surface: Emetics act precisely like this, with expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Emetics are drugs that cause vomiting, so they make people feel ill.

clue.text: Manege for Yorkshire swimmers?

parts.note: Yorkshire was historically divided into three ridings
a school is a group of fish swimming together

explanation.surface: An arena for Yorkshire swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: A manege is an arena where horses are trained, so the answer is a place where people learn horsemanship.
explanation.definitionFit: A manege is an enclosed area for training horses and riders.

clue.text: Muscle is crisp, then floppy

indicators.note: floppy means limp and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A muscle that is crisp, then goes limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floppy' rearranges the letters of CRISP THEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphincter is a ring of muscle that closes an opening in the body.

clue.text: You chaps turn the top of the heating system

indicators.note: turn means the letters of you chaps are rearranged
top of means the first letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the men should take a turn adjusting the heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges YOU CHAPS; 'top of' gives T from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypocaust was a Roman underfloor heating system using hot air.

clue.text: Suggest giving support to sterling?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, giving support to
the pound is the unit of British currency, sterling

explanation.surface: Proposing to prop up the British pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound an idea is to put it forward for consideration.

clue.text: British writer to form crew — playing chicken?

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a risky game of nerve

parts.note: ink is what a pen writes with
to man a ship is to form its crew
to man a ship is to form its crew

explanation.surface: A British author forms a crew, perhaps to play a game of dare.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing a dangerous situation to the very edge to make an opponent back down first.

clue.text: See 13
A system we all have that an emperor holds against us

definitions.note: a description; the adjective names the body system every person has

indicators.note: holds means the emperor's name contains the letter for against

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor
v is short for versus, against
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everyone has a system, which a Roman emperor turns against us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts V, the versus of sports fixtures, inside the emperor; the definition reads cryptically as the system we all share.
explanation.definitionFit: Every human body has a network of nerves carrying signals, called the nervous system.

clue.text: Offence against the state loses initiator, and why

indicators.note: losing its initiator means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: treason is betraying one's country

explanation.surface: A treasonable act drops its instigator, and someone asks why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses initiator' takes the T off TREASON.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is the cause or explanation, the answer to why.

clue.text: Spaniel with front part almost exactly the same

clue.text: Contribution of Russian by inversion

indicators.note: inversion here means the two halves of the Russian's name swap places

parts.note: Vladimir Putin is the Russian president

explanation.surface: A Russian making his contribution by turning things upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by inversion' swaps PUT and IN in PUTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is something put in, a contribution to a discussion or task.

clue.text: Dress circle used to be in cinema

parts.note: garb means clothing, dress
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: The dress circle used to be in the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: Greta Garbo was a Swedish film star of the 1920s and 30s.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a film star who retired from the screen in 1941.

clue.text: See 26
Shoe for a sovereign and five cents for bread

parts.note: a pump is a light slip-on shoe
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
a nickel is an American five-cent coin

explanation.surface: Swapping a shoe for a gold coin, and small change for a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpernickel is a dark German rye loaf.

clue.text: Eruption directed to Brutus

indicators.note: directed, as a stage director arranges actors, signals the letters of to Brutus are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry eruption aimed at Brutus, as in Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: An outburst is a sudden explosion of emotion, an eruption.

clue.text: Offence against the state with first to last variations

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is moved to the end

parts.note: sedition is incitement against the state's authority

explanation.surface: Variants of an anti-government crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with first to last' moves the S of SEDITION to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Different editions of a text are versions differing from one another.

clue.text: Eyepiece for Maigret in action

indicators.note: for here means supplied by: the letters come from within the run Maigret in action

explanation.surface: An eyeglass for Simenon's detective Maigret at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the words 'Maigret in action', with 'for' pointing to them as its source.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.
